finding.claim: The public POST /hooks/test endpoint sends a server-side request to a user-supplied callback URL. It has no URL validation and no authentication in this file, so it is a full SSRF. An attacker can reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints. The response status is returned, which gives an oracle for probing internal hosts.

trace.note: pub router is created with no auth middleware
the value is passed directly to axios.post
the upstream status code is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme, host or allowlist check. No private/loopback/link-local IP blocking. No DNS-rebind protection. axios follows redirects by default. requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router (routes.js:12), not to pub. I could not see where pub is mounted, since only routes.js exists, so any auth applied at mount time is unverified.

verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 passes req.body.callback straight to axios.post and returns the upstream status with no validation. requireAdmin is applied only to the admin router (routes.js:12), so pub is not admin-gated. Mount-time authentication could not be checked because only routes.js exists, but any low-privilege caller could still reach the sink.

finding.claim: The GET /diagnostics/fetch endpoint fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL server-side with no validation. It is gated by admin role, which lowers severity but does not remove the SSRF. A compromised or malicious admin can reach internal networks and metadata services, and the issue can be chained with session or role compromise.

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) guards every route on the admin router
req.query.url is passed directly to axios.get
the upstream status code is returned

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10) checks req.session.role === 'admin', and this works as authorization. There is no URL scheme, host or allowlist validation. There is no private-IP blocking. Redirects are followed.

verdict.guard_found: requireAdmin (routes.js:7-10, applied at routes.js:12) restricts the route to session role 'admin'. There is no URL validation.
verdict.reason: The trace lines are accurate (routes.js:12-16), but req.query.url at routes.js:15 is only reachable through admin.use(requireAdmin) at routes.js:12, which returns 403 unless the session role is admin (routes.js:8). A low-privilege or unauthenticated attacker therefore cannot control the source; the finding would only hold with a separate admin-session compromise.
